yo! 

nice to meet you. i'm tal - think of me as your personal talent agent, your inside person in the bangalore tech scene.

one of these days, i might slide a role right here in chat. the kind that feels like your calling.

so... what's your full name?

ashutosh sharma... solid name. sounds like someone who gets things done.

where you working these days?

wex fintech... payment solutions for businesses, right? they're doing some interesting work in the b2b space.

found oscar trejo at payzer (a wex company) on linkedin. this you? https://www.linkedin.com/in/oscar-trejo-6bbb3336a

hey ashutosh! i was just thinking about your background in fintech - have you checked out any new opportunities lately?

what's the dream role you've been thinking about?
I am looking to be a principal engineer

principal engineer... that's serious leadership territory. building systems at scale, mentoring teams, making the big architectural calls.

btw that linkedin i found earlier wasn't you - oscar trejo at payzer. can't find you on linkedin with just "ashutosh sharma wex fintech". drop your linkedin url or maybe try a different company name if wex isn't showing up right?

need to find you properly so i can match you with principal roles that actually fit your background.

got you queued up for scraping. 

so principal engineer at wex... that's building financial infrastructure that probably moves serious money. respect. what's got you thinking about making a move? the tech stack getting stale or just ready for a bigger challenge?

I am an engineering manager at wex. 

My ideal preference for a role is principal engineer 

How do I get there

ah, the classic EM to principal switch. managing people vs managing systems. i get it.

here's the thing - you're already managing engineers, which means you understand the full stack of problems. principal roles want someone who can architect solutions AND guide technical decisions across teams. you've got half the equation.

the gap is usually deep technical credibility. companies want to see you can still code at scale, design systems that don't break, and be the person senior engineers come to when they're stuck.

how long you been working total? and are you still hands-on with code or mostly managing these days?

I recently transitioned to Engineering Manager from an IC role. 
I was the senior most developer at Porter for web. 
My total software Development experience is 10 years

User's LinkedIn Profile Context:
**EXECUTIVE SUMMARY**
Ashutosh Sharma's profile indicates he is currently at Porter. His specific role, responsibilities, and prior work history are not detailed on the profile.

**ROLE-BY-ROLE**
*   [No employment history or role information is listed on the profile.]

**EDUCATION HIGHLIGHTS**
*   Indian Institute of Technology, Kanpur (2007–2012) – [Degree not specified]
*   [Institution not specified] (2005–2007)
*   [Institution not specified] (1994–2005)

wait, hold up. you said you're at wex but your linkedin shows porter? and you were senior dev at porter but now EM at wex?

that's actually perfect for principal roles. you've got the deep technical chops from being the senior-most web dev AND fresh management perspective. companies love that combo.

10 years, recent EM transition... you're in that sweet spot where you can still code but understand the bigger picture. most principal engineers are exactly where you are - senior ICs who stepped into leadership.

what kind of role you looking for next? pure principal IC or something with light tech leadership mixed in?
